content.summary: Exact integer recomputation confirms the two-star bound and Profile A count window. The incidence argument attains its largest numerical residual allowance only at overlap nine. A deliberate weakening of the other-point degree cap shows why the inherited at-most-two-high-points result is a necessary input to this particular eighty-bound argument.

checks.scope: Two-star incidence arithmetic and assumption robustness
checks.method: Read TwoHighIncidence.lean and enumerated all integer overlaps q from zero through twelve using the two stated inequalities; repeated the calculation after weakening the noncenter degree cap from nineteen to twenty. Exact output retained in scratch/domain_expert/round05_arithmetic.json.
checks.observation: The weighted combination is 37m at most 1512, while 37 times 41 is 1517. The integer overlap caps are 0,4,9,13,18,22,27,31,36,40,39,37,36, so m=40 requires q=9 in this relaxation. Empty overlap and coincident supports produce no unhandled endpoint. Weakening the noncenter degree cap changes residual caps to fifteen and ten and permits m=45 numerically; the actual degree-nineteen argument is therefore substantive and is correctly supplied by the unconditional high-point cap. These are relaxation bounds, not realizability or sharpness claims.

checks.scope: Profile A outsider census and disjoint-completion thresholds
checks.method: Recomputed the meeting inequality and enumerated nonnegative integer census triples satisfying n0+n1+n2=61, n1+2n2=76, n2 at most 27 and n0 at least nine.
checks.observation: For a two-outsider member the degree sum is 66; 2|M|+2 at most 106 gives |M| at most 52 and at least nine of the 61 residual members disjoint from it. The only census triples (n0,n1,n2) are (9,28,24), (10,26,25), (11,24,26), (12,22,27). All satisfy n2 at least 24, making the final at-most-twenty contradiction strict with margin at least four.
